children: Diabetes and obesity-drug maker Eli Lilly

traded at $1,284.51, down approximately 1.70% at 10.09am EST, on October 23. With earnings due next Thursday, according to Reuters' earnings preview, the key question is whether surging demand can keep overpowering weaker pricing.

Lilly's second-quarter results put that tension in numbers: revenue climbed 48% to $23 billion as volume increased 60%, while realized prices declined 13%. Mounjaro and Zepbound generated roughly $14.9 billion combined. Management raised its full-year revenue outlook to $85 billion$87 billion, setting a demanding benchmark for the next report.

The valuation picture shows shares 19.01% below the GF Value estimate of roughly $1,590, suggesting potential upside against that model rather than a guaranteed bargain. Demand is powerful. Turning it into profitable growth remains the test. Investors should watch realized pricing, gross margin and manufacturing progress to judge whether higher prescription volumes are delivering enough earnings power.

title: Eli Lilly Stocks Slip 1.7% Ahead of Earnings After 48% Revenue Growth
